title: Table cleanup drops active lists after an unsuccessful catalog read
severity_basis: Source review: seeded list tables containing data are deleted under confirmed SQL-read failure. Frequency and on-device incidence are unknown.
environment: Actual model.cpp/undoremove.cpp compiled in a temporary Qt 6.12 MSVC x64 probe. Each run creates a fresh in-memory SQLite database; no personal database or application installation is used.
source: Model::dropRemovedTables collects catalog rows without checking initial or iteration errors, then reuses the query for sqlite_master and deletes UUID tables absent from the incomplete collection.
evidence: Initial failure fixture: catalog view lacks the required id column. Read returns no rows with a valid SQL error; componentComplete drops both seeded active list tables and the orphan.

Iteration failure fixture: required id projection raises SQLite integer overflow on the second catalog row. exec succeeds, one row is read, then lastError is valid; cleanup preserves the first active table but drops the second active table and orphan.
Healthy complete-catalog control preserves both active tables and removes only the orphan.
Read-only control under the partial-read fault preserves all three tables.
expected: Only classify tables as orphaned after a complete successful catalog read. On a read error, retain every existing table and its contents, report the error and abort cleanup. An error-free empty catalog remains a valid cleanup input.
reproduction: Create a memory database with two catalog identities, two associated UUID-named tables containing rows, and an orphan UUID table.
Inject an initial read failure or an error fetching the second required ID through a catalog view; independently verify exec/row/error state.
Create the production Model and call componentComplete, which invokes dropRemovedTables.
Inspect sqlite_master: active tables missing from the incomplete read have been dropped. Repeat healthy/read-only controls.
scope_limits: This is deterministic fault injection at the Model boundary, not an observed phone incident or full-app failure reproduction. main.cpp checks the initial catalog exec during startup; that does not establish protection against a later/partial Model read failure. The injected views are test fixtures, not the normal app schema.

regression.before: Both faulted-read preservation checks fail (exit 1); healthy and read-only controls pass (exit 0). Logs record query state and surviving tables.
regression.permanent_test_required: Completed: both fault scenarios fail in normal QTest before/pass after; controls verify retained data and intended healthy cleanup.
regression.permanent_before: 5 records pass, 2 fail because active tables are missing after initial/iteration failure. Controls pass.
regression.permanent_after: All 7 focused records pass; preserved table contents/UUIDs and healthy/empty/read-only policies checked.

implementation_scope: Selected read-validation fix plus permanent QTest regression/documentation. Check catalog lastError after iteration and return before table inventory/DROP on failure; storage schema and cleanup membership logic retained.

resolution.change: After catalog iteration, check query.lastError and report/return on error before the query is reused or any table inventory/drop occurs. Existing read-only guard, membership algorithm and schema remain.
resolution.before: 5 records pass, 2 fail on missing active tables after initial and mid-iteration catalog faults. Healthy/read-only/empty controls pass.
resolution.after: All 7 focused records pass. Verify table existence, names, checked flags and UUIDs; failed reads retain all seeded tables, healthy cleanup removes only orphans, empty/read-only policies retained.

verification.limits: Actual Model/SQLite fault injection establishes cleanup safety, not an observed phone incident, corrupt-file repair or general loading-error recovery. Existing full app interactions run offscreen; no new Android/native rendering certification.

resolution.commit: Committed with this ticket's source changes and permanent regression tests; see Git history and DEV-006 closure.
